title: China-to-Montenegro EV Charger Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Connector Interoperability — GB/T 20234 vs IEC 62196 Type 2 / CCS2
rows.target_requirement: Montenegro charging deployments are typically in the European connector family, and infrastructure is commonly expected to follow IEC 62196 Type 2 AC for AC charging and IEC 62196-3 CCS2 for DC fast charging where local project procurement or fleet requirements specify it. Exporters should treat connector selection as a project and compatibility question, not standalone evidence of market compliance.
target_standards: IEC 61851-1 — EV conductive charging general requirements
rows.china_equivalent: Chinese AC chargers commonly use GB/T 20234.2 and DC chargers GB/T 20234.3. These are not directly plug-compatible with IEC Type 2 or CCS2 in connector geometry, locking, and signaling behavior. GB/T DC also uses GB/T 27930 communication instead of IEC CCS2 communication expectations.
rows.gap: A GB/T-only charger is not connector-ready for practical Montenegro deployments. Conversion requires coupler and cable redesign, lock and temperature-rise evidence, control pilot implementation, DC communication alignment where CCS2 is used, labels, spare parts, and IEC test evidence.

mandatory_status.target: Project-dependent but practically mandatory where the importer, charge-point operator, vehicle fleet, or port corridor specification requires Type 2 or CCS2
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 20234 conformity applies to China domestic connector design and is not a direct IEC Type 2 / CCS2 substitute

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Connector compatibility is a hardware and protocol requirement. Confirm Type 2 / CCS2 compatibility before shipment; GB/T connectors should not be treated as an admissible Montenegro plug-ready configuration.

rows.requirement: CGES Grid Connection — 230/400 V, 50 Hz and Utility Coordination
rows.target_requirement: Montenegro uses a 230/400 V, 50 Hz low-voltage supply. Grid-connected EV charger installations should be coordinated with the Eswatini Electricity Company equivalent operator CGES and with REGAGEN where licensing, tariff, network, or sector approval questions arise. Local utility coordination usually includes load assessment, protection coordination, metering, and site commissioning documentation.
target_standards: CGES grid-connection and supply coordination requirements
IEC 61000 series — EMC and power-quality context
rows.china_equivalent: China domestic charger installations are commonly documented against GB/T 18487.1-2023, GB/T 20234 connectors, GB/T 27930 for DC communication, and local grid-operator acceptance. China domestic supply is commonly 220 V single-phase / 380 V three-phase, 50 Hz; Montenegro’s 230/400 V, 50 Hz requires project-level matching of voltage range and utility settings.
china_standards: China local grid operator project-acceptance requirements
rows.gap: Exporters should confirm input ratings cover 230 V single-phase and 400 V three-phase at 50 Hz, prepare single-line diagrams and load calculations, document harmonic and EMC performance, confirm protective-device coordination, and obtain project-specific CGES and REGAGEN guidance before shipment or activation.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory project gate: grid-connected installations require CGES supply coordination and may require REGAGEN approval depending on site, tariff, and network impact
mandatory_status.cn: China local grid-operator acceptance applies domestically and is not a CGES or REGAGEN substitute

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat CGES grid coordination as a project gate. A China domestic charger package must be checked for 230/400 V, 50 Hz ratings, protection coordination, harmonic and EMC evidence, and project utility requirements before installation in Montenegro.

rows.requirement: SWASA-style Market Access and Conformity Assessment Scope
rows.target_requirement: Import and market-readiness checks for EV chargers in Montenegro should confirm HS code, product category, coupler accessories, rated voltage, wireless or network functions, labels, and document route before shipment. For grid-connected chargers, conformity and interconnection are handled separately from local utility and regulator reviews.
target_standards: CGES grid-connection coordination for installed chargers
rows.china_equivalent: China-market chargers are documented under GB/T 18487.1-2023, GB/T 20234 connectors, GB/T 27930 for DC communication, and CCC where in scope. China documents are useful for technical comparison but do not automatically establish Montenegro market access.
rows.gap: Before claiming readiness for Montenegro, exporters should map importer, customs path, conformity route, IEC safety and EMC reports, Type 2 / CCS2 connector configuration, English labels and manuals, wireless/network functions, spare parts, and any utility-route requirements including Bar port documentation.

mandatory_status.target: Conditional to mandatory depending on product scope — importer documents, customs, utility and regulator reviews should be confirmed for the exact charger and project before shipment
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory or recommended depending on China CCC scope; GB/T or CCC evidence is not a Montenegro customs or market substitute

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not infer Montenegro market access from China GB/T or CCC files alone. Confirm the importer and regulator route, customs path, utility coordination, and any Bar-port logistics requirement before shipping.

rows.requirement: Montenegro EV Market Context — Maritime Corridor Through Bar
rows.target_requirement: Montenegro is a small market with significant import logistics through Bar for corridor shipments. Early EV charger deployments can be fleet, hospitality, tourism, and cross-border project-based rather than a nationwide public network. This makes connector and utility compatibility important, but does not replace project approvals.
target_standards: Vehicle fleet and project-specific compatibility expectations
rows.china_equivalent: China’s EV charging market is large and standards-driven around GB/T connectors and GB/T 27930 communication. Scale in China does not remove the need for Montenegro-specific hardware, labels, documentation, and project approvals.
china_standards: New Energy Vehicle Industry Development Plan 2021-2035 (China)
rows.gap: Treat Montenegro market context as a demand signal, not a compliance shortcut. Confirm fleet mix, corridor routing, CGES interconnection, and customs/port requirements before bidding or contracting. Project-level specifications often override general assumptions.

mandatory_status.target: Policy and market context — not itself a mandatory product standard; utility and regulator routes remain separate gates
mandatory_status.cn: Policy context only — China EV policy and GB/T market maturity do not affect Montenegro conformity or project obligations

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Montenegro context and Bar corridor assumptions should guide specifications, but project confirmation from importer, operator, and regulator remains the prerequisite for shipment and installation readiness.

source.publisher: Government of Montenegro transport and logistics authority references

rows.requirement: OCPP Readiness, EMC, and Power-Quality Evidence
rows.target_requirement: OCPP requirements in Montenegro are typically project-driven rather than a single published national EVSE protocol mandate. Networked public chargers should be prepared for OCPP interoperability, remote monitoring, metering data exchange, fault reporting, and load management. EMC and power-quality evidence should be based on IEC 61000-family testing and coordinated with CGES requirements for the connection point.
target_standards: OCPP interoperability context for networked chargers
CGES and REGAGEN project oversight where network operation issues arise
rows.china_equivalent: China DC chargers commonly implement GB/T 27930 between charger and battery management system. That stack is not a direct substitute for OCPP interoperability and is not equivalent to CCS2/IEC communication requirements. Chinese EMC reports may need reassessment against Montenegro site conditions and CGES coordination.
rows.gap: Exporters should confirm the required OCPP version and cybersecurity expectations in each Montenegro project, test remote monitoring and fault reporting with the intended operator, prepare IEC 61000 EMC and harmonic evidence, and document load-management functions for the CGES connection point.

mandatory_status.target: Project-dependent where required by the charge-point operator, public charging tender, fleet owner, or network-management specification; EMC and power-quality evidence are expected for grid coordination
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 27930 is China domestic DC vehicle-to-charger communication and is not an OCPP or IEC substitute

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] For networked chargers in Montenegro, confirm project-level OCPP and remote-management requirements and prepare IEC 61000 EMC and power-quality evidence for utility coordination. GB/T 27930 alone does not satisfy these needs.

rows.requirement: IEC 61851 Safety Baseline and CGES Conformity Evidence
rows.target_requirement: For EV charging equipment in Montenegro, exporters should prepare IEC-family evidence suitable for regulatory review at the project and utility level. IEC 61851-1 provides baseline requirements for conductive charging, and IEC 61851-23 covers DC EV supply equipment. Site documentation should also include enclosure protection, installation instructions, markings, and environment-assurance evidence.
target_standards: IEC 61851-1 — safety of conductive EV supply equipment
rows.china_equivalent: China comparable safety baseline is GB/T 18487.1-2023, used with GB/T connector and communication standards. It can support engineering comparison, but China evidence is not equivalent to Montenegro IEC 61851 evidence for ISME/REGAGEN/CGES or project-owner review.
rows.gap: Exporters should prepare IEC 61851 evidence for the exact model, including protective-device ratings, earthing, isolation, emergency-stop and safe-disconnection descriptions, enclosure IP evidence, English documentation, and explicit mapping from Chinese evidence to IEC clauses.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where CGES and project owner confirm ISME- or IEC-based safety evidence is required for the grid-connected model and use case
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 18487 applies to Chinese design and is not direct IEC 61851 evidence for Montenegro without additional assessment

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Build Montenegro EV charger files around IEC 61851 evidence and project-specific regulatory review, using China GB/T documents only as mapped references. Verify site acceptance criteria before claiming readiness.
